evidence.notes: Local Database.getDeleted returns tombstoned records whose deleted timestamp falls inside the requested sync window.
GetDeletedResult exposes matching local DeletedRecord DTOs.
DeletedRecord exposes the deleted local record Id.
DeletedRecord exposes the deleted local record Id.
DeletedRecord exposes the local deletion DateTime.
DeletedRecord exposes the local deletion DateTime.

source.content: @isTest private class DatabaseDeletedSyncWindowFixtureTest { @isTest static void deletedWindowReturnsMatchingRecords() { Account account = new Account(Name = 'Delete Me'); insert account; Id accountId = account.Id; delete account; Datetime startWindow = Datetime.newInstanceGmt(2026, 5, 2, 11, 59, 0); Datetime endWindow = Datetime.newInstanceGmt(2026, 5, 2, 12, 5, 0); Database.GetDeletedResult inside = Database.getDeleted('Account', startWindow, endWindow); System.assertEquals(1, inside.getDeletedRecords().size()); Database.DeletedRecord deleted = inside.getDeletedRecords()[0]; System.assertEquals(accountId, deleted.getId()); System.assertNotEquals(null, deleted.getDeletedDate()); System.assertEquals(startWindow, inside.getEarliestDateAvailable()); System.assertEquals(endWindow, inside.getLatestDateCovered()); Database.GetDeletedResult outside = Database.getDeleted('Account', Datetime.newInstanceGmt(2026, 5, 1, 0, 0, 0), Datetime.newInstanceGmt(2026, 5, 1, 1, 0, 0)); System.assertEquals(0, outside.getDeletedRecords().size()); } }
